reason: Both requested outputs rest on an inventory induction (nitrogenAfter k = q*feed*sum_i q^{2i}) that multiplies the surviving nitrogen by q = 1 - eta a second time when recycled material re-enters the reactor, so each cycle applies the conversion factor twice. The four printed steps contain no loss or conversion at the re-entry step: fresh feed and recycled gases mix unreactive, then the reaction converts fraction eta = 0.150 once per cycle (constant per-cycle yield), ammonia is removed once, and the unreacted remainder is returned. The recurrence implied by the printed steps is N_{k+1} = q*(N_k + n0/4), which for n0 = 4 mol gives N_58 = 4.2497 mol to 4 d.p. — not 3.0631 mol. The candidate's answer interpretations are also internally inconsistent under its own model: its part (b) Y(n) = 1 - q^n treats each material parcel as converted in one pass per cycle (Y(1) = 0.150), but the very first cycle of its part (a) induction already requires two passes for the fresh portion (N_1 = q^2*(n0/4) at k>=2, i.e. 15% 'single-pass' yield but 27.75% first-cycle conversion). Because the geometric-progression-hinted recurrence has a text-compatible alternative (A_k = q*A_{k-1} + n0/4 giving A_58 = 5.6662 mol) and the source itself is ambiguous between single- and double-conversion readings while hinting at the 1 - q^k form, the submitted answer cannot be established from the printed data.
